summary:
# NASA Space Mission Design Game

The NASA Space Mission Design Game is an educational and interactive project where students act as NASA mission planners and design their own space exploration missions using real NASA data and engineering concepts.

Participants choose one of three destinations: Mars, Titan, or Europa. They design a spacecraft by planning its propulsion, power, communication, navigation, life-support, and scientific instrument systems.

Each team receives a hypothetical budget of 100 mission credits, which they must manage wisely. During the game, teams face real spaceflight challenges such as solar radiation, communication delays, extreme temperatures, space debris, and equipment failures.

Students work in teams of 4–5 members, develop solutions, and present their final mission designs. Their performance is evaluated on scientific accuracy, spacecraft design, resource management, problem-solving, and teamwork.

The project aims to develop creativity, scientific knowledge, engineering skills, and teamwork while making space exploration exciting and practical.
details:
NASA SPACE MISSION DESIGN GAME

Design Your Mission. Explore the Universe.

1. Introduction

Our project is based on the NASA Space Mission Design Game. The main idea of this project is to make learning about space exploration more interesting and practical. In this game, students act as NASA mission planners and get a chance to design their own space missions.

Instead of only reading about planets and spacecraft, students take part in different activities where they have to make decisions, manage resources, and solve problems. The game is based on real NASA information and space engineering concepts.

2. Objective of the Project

The main objective of our project is to help students understand how a space mission works and what things are required to make it successful.

Through this game, students can learn about different planets, spacecraft systems, space technology, and the challenges faced during space exploration. It also helps improve teamwork, creativity, decision-making, and problem-solving skills.

3. Choosing a Mission Destination

In our game, participants can choose one destination from three real places in our solar system.

Mars: Mars is the fourth planet from the Sun. It has a thin atmosphere mainly made of carbon dioxide. NASA's Perseverance rover is exploring Mars to study its surface and search for signs of ancient life.

Titan: Titan is the largest moon of Saturn. It has a thick atmosphere and lakes of liquid methane and ethane. NASA's Dragonfly mission is planned to explore this moon.

Europa: Europa is one of Jupiter's moons. It has an icy surface and strong evidence of an ocean beneath it. NASA's Europa Clipper mission is studying this moon to understand whether it has conditions suitable for life.

Each team has to choose one destination and plan its mission accordingly.

4. Designing the Spacecraft

After selecting a destination, participants have to think about what type of spacecraft will be needed for the mission.

They have to understand six important systems:

  • Propulsion System: Helps the spacecraft move and control its direction.
  • Power System: Provides electricity to operate different equipment.
  • Communication System: Helps the spacecraft send and receive information from Earth.
  • Navigation System: Helps determine the spacecraft's position and direction.
  • Life Support System: Provides breathable air and manages water for crewed missions.
  • Scientific Instruments: Help collect information and study the selected destination.

All these systems are important for planning a successful mission.

5. Resource Management

Another important part of our game is resource management. Every team gets a total of 100 mission credits.

Teams have to use these credits for different requirements, such as fuel, propulsion, communication, navigation, scientific instruments, and safety systems.

They cannot spend unlimited credits, so they have to make smart decisions. For example, spending too many credits on one system may leave fewer credits for other important systems.

This activity teaches students how to manage limited resources.

The 100 credits are part of our game rules and do not represent an actual NASA budget.

6. Space Mission Challenges

During a space mission, many unexpected problems can happen. To make our game more interesting, we have included different challenges based on real spaceflight risks.

Some examples are:

  • Solar radiation and space weather.
  • Communication failure or signal loss.
  • Extreme temperatures.
  • Space debris and collision risks.
  • Limited power supply.
  • Equipment malfunction.

When a team faces a challenge, its members have to discuss the problem and find a suitable solution using their available resources.

7. Game Rules

The game is played in a few simple steps:

  1. Students form teams of 4–5 members.
  2. Each team selects Mars, Titan, or Europa.
  3. Teams design their spacecraft.
  4. They distribute their 100 mission credits.
  5. They plan their mission and scientific objectives.
  6. They solve unexpected space challenges.
  7. Finally, they present their mission plan to the judges.

8. Scoring System

At the end of the game, every team is evaluated out of 100 points.

  • Scientific Accuracy – 25 points.
  • Spacecraft Design – 20 points.
  • Resource Management – 20 points.
  • Problem Solving – 20 points.
  • Teamwork and Presentation – 15 points.

The team that performs best and gets the highest score will be declared the winner.

9. Benefits of the Project

This project helps students learn about space in a more practical way. It improves their knowledge of science and technology and teaches them how to work in a team.

It also develops creative thinking, decision-making, communication, and problem-solving skills. Most importantly, students get an idea of how scientists and engineers plan real space missions.

10. Conclusion

Overall, the NASA Space Mission Design Game is a fun and educational way to learn about space exploration. It gives students an opportunity to think like real mission planners and understand the different things involved in sending a spacecraft into space.

Through this game, students can learn, share ideas, work together, and solve different challenges. Our aim is to make space science easier to understand and more interesting for everyone.

"The next great space mission could begin with your idea!"
